Q: Setting the statement name in PDO Prepared Statements (MySQL/MariaDB) A:

I made an experiment to do what you describe, re-using a prepared statement in subsequent PHP requests.

I can't do it with PDO::prepare() and PDOStatement::execute(), because as the comments above describe, those create a PHP resource that gets cleaned up at the end of each HTTP request.

But it does work if I use PREPARE and EXECUTE, the SQL protocol method of using prepared statements.

<?php

$pdo = new PDO("mysql:host=localhost;dbname=test;charset=utf8mb4",
  "root", "password",
  [PDO::ATTR_PERSISTENT=>true]);

# $pdo->exec("PREPARE stmt FROM 'SELECT * FROM mytable'");

$stmt = $pdo->query("EXECUTE stmt");
$result = $stmt->fetchAll(PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);

...display however you want...

I ran the script once with the PREPARE uncommented, and then subsequently commented out that line in the PHP script (as shown above). Then I reload the page in my browser, and successfully saw that the prepared query can be re-executed by its name stmt.

I would not choose to do this in a real application. One problem is that this script never deallocates the prepared query, which is a known way to cause a resource leak in MySQL Server.

Also, I don't think the performance gain of reusing the query in subsequent requests would be great enough to warrant rewriting prepared queries in this way and sacrificing use of the PDO methods.

Frankly, if you were writing an app for which even micro-optimizations of performance were that important, you wouldn't be writing it in PHP.

Q: How to test react form onSubmit with formik and react testing library? A:

Your SignUpForm doesn't have an onSubmit prop.

If your onSubmit comes from another file, you should mock the function in that module.

import * as HelperFunctions from './submitForm.js'

At the start of your test, you can spy on that function.

jest.spyOn(HelperFunctions, 'onSubmit')

then you can test if it is being called like so.

expect(HelperFunctions.onSubmit).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      email: "john.dee@someemail.com",
      firstName: "John",
      lastName: "Dee",
      password: "password",
    })

make sure the functions are exported.
